story.head: Stone’s favorite opponent
paras: The Golden Knights won the teams’ first meeting this season, 2-1 in overtime in Vegas on Oct 10. The Kings have won two in a row, while the Golden Knights (15-7-5) lost 4-1 to San Jose on Friday. This is a Pacific Division matchup, with the Knights second (sixth in the NHL) and the Kings seventh (29th). The Pacific has been the weakest of the four divisions so far.

The Golden Knights’ record (.648) is about what their chances are worth. The Kings have played better than their record (.435) says: their chances are worth about .593, and their finishing has held them back.

This season, the Golden Knights have outscored teams 89-79, even though they’ve been outscored 56-55 at 5-on-5. On special teams, they’ve outscored teams 27-16. This season, the Kings have been outscored 74-64, but only 41-38 at 5-on-5. On special teams, opponents have outscored them 22-17.

The Golden Knights draw more penalties than they take (1st), have one of the league’s best penalty kills (3rd) and create chances on the penalty kill (3rd). The Kings keep dangerous shots away better than anyone (1st), but take a lot of low-quality shots (28th). The Golden Knights’ power play against the Kings’ penalty killers is strength against strength, and the Golden Knights have the edge over the Kings on shots from defensemen.

Jack Eichel (12 G / 22 A / 34 P in 27 GP) leads the Golden Knights in scoring and is tied for seventh in the NHL, with seven points in his last five games. Mitch Marner (4 G / 26 A / 30 P in 25 GP) is next in line, with a point in six straight games against Los Angeles. For the Kings, Artemi Panarin (8 G / 13 A / 21 P in 19 GP) leads the way in scoring, with a point in six straight games against Vegas. Adrian Kempe (7 G / 8 A / 15 P in 22 GP) isn’t far behind.
Carter Hart (8-5-2 / .887 SV% in 15 GS) will likely start for Vegas, and Darcy Kuemper (9-5-1 / .891 SV% in 15 GS) for Los Angeles.
